title: UP delays draft voter roll to 17 November amid row over Yogi's 'missing Hindu voters'
dek: Voters dropped in the SIR are told they can re-enrol on Form 6 without fear of prosecution. The Samajwadi Party asks how the Chief Minister knows the religion of missing voters.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Uttar Pradesh's election office has put back publication of the draft electoral roll for the 2027 Assembly election by five days, to 17 November, and has told voters who were left off the rolls during this year's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) that they can apply again without facing prosecution. The steps come as Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's claim that 1.27 crore Hindu voters are missing from the rolls has set off a fight with the Samajwadi Party (SP).

The draft roll had been due on Thursday, 12 November. Under the revised schedule for the Special Summary Revision, which covers all 403 Assembly constituencies, claims and objections on Forms 6, 7 and 8 will be accepted from 17 November to 16 December, instead of until 11 December. The date for deciding them stays at 28 December, giving officials less time, and the final roll will be published on 4 January 2027, with 1 January 2027 as the qualifying date, according to reports.

## Re-enrolling 'without fear'

Announcing the changes on Tuesday, UP Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa said electors who were on the roll before the SIR but are missing from it now can file Form 6, the form for new voters, according to reports. No action under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, which punishes false declarations, "shall be initiated merely on the ground that an elector was previously registered", he said, provided the applicant is not registered in another constituency. District election officers have been told to publicise this. The Election Commission of India gave a similar assurance for other states on 3 November.

The scale is large. Uttar Pradesh had about 15.44 crore electors before the SIR. The final roll published on 11 April 2026 had 13,39,84,792, after more than 2.04 crore names were removed and 84.28 lakh added, according to reports. The state election office has also told district officers to compare Assembly rolls with panchayat and urban local body voter lists.

## The Chief Minister's claim

In a television interview last weekend, Mr Adityanath said that a comparison of Assembly rolls with panchayat voter lists showed about 1.27 crore Hindu voters were missing, along with about 4.5 lakh voters aged 18 or 19, according to reports. The state government has asked for a review. Mr Adityanath accused the Opposition of spreading misinformation about the SIR and urged the Commission to include all eligible voters and remove the names of dead voters and those he called infiltrators, reports said.

The Election Commission has not publicly responded to the 1.27 crore figure.

## What the Opposition says

SP president Akhilesh Yadav has questioned how the figure was arrived at. "The question arises: How do they know that the names of Hindu voters are missing?" he said, adding: "It appears that the Election Commission has shared the entire data with the chief minister or the chief minister's office." The SP wants Aadhaar-linked voting and biometric checks at polling stations.

Nationally, the Congress-led INDIA bloc is demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the SIR. Congress general secretary K.C. Venugopal said on Sunday that the party would continue its campaign until he is removed. Union Home Minister Amit Shah has offered to discuss the opposition's concerns in a special session of Parliament.

## What happens next

The draft roll for Uttar Pradesh will be published on 17 November, and claims and objections can be filed until 16 December. The final roll is due on 4 January 2027, ahead of an Assembly election expected early that year. Rolls in several other states, including Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Haryana, are due on 30 November, and Delhi's on 22 December.
